title: Madlab - The Ultimate Innovation Hackathon
description: MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon About the Opportunity MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking. This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas. Eligibility Criteria Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship. Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome. Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed). Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged). No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills. Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions. Team Formation Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members. Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists. Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes. Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact. Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers. Competition Format and Rounds Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes) Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge. Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes) Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies. Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team) Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently. Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team) Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally. Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling. Problem Statements Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas: Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem. Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan. Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model. Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution. The final problem statement, required deliverables, and evaluation criteria will be communicated to participants before the relevant round begins. Evaluation Criteria Participants will be evaluated on the following criteria: Creativity and originality — 20% Problem-solving and practical execution — 20% Technical or domain-specific skills — 20% Communication and presentation — 15% Marketing, sales, and business thinking — 15% Teamwork, adaptability, and Q&A performance — 10% Judges' decisions will be final, subject to the event's published rules. Competition Rules All submissions must be created or substantially developed by the participating team during the competition, unless the organizers explicitly permit pre-existing resources. Pre-existing code, templates, AI tools, and third-party resources may be used only as permitted by the organizers. Teams must disclose significant external contributions. Plagiarism, copied submissions presented as original work, fabricated results, impersonation, and misrepresentation of contributions are prohibited. Every team member must contribute meaningfully to the competition. Participants must respect fellow competitors, judges, mentors, volunteers, and organizers. Teams must submit their deliverables before the announced deadline. Late submissions may be penalized or disqualified. Participants must not attempt unauthorized access to systems, misuse personal data, or engage in unethical or illegal activities. All presentations must be professional, relevant to the assigned challenge, and completed within the allocated time. Participants must follow the venue's safety requirements and the organizers' instructions throughout the event. Any disputes, rule violations, or exceptional circumstances will be reviewed by the organizing committee. Deliverables Each team must submit the relevant deliverables for its assigned challenge, which may include: A working prototype, demonstration, campaign concept, sales pitch, or business solution. A short explanation of the problem and the proposed solution. A presentation outlining the approach, target audience, execution plan, and expected impact. Supporting materials such as designs, mock-ups, code, campaign creatives, or a business model, where applicable. Final Note MADLAB is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and demonstrate what you can create, communicate, build, market, and sell. Whether you are a developer, marketer, salesperson, designer, or business thinker, your skills have a place in the lab. Bring your creativity. Challenge the ordinary. Execute the extraordinary. MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution. Note: The organizers should confirm the final team size, eligibility, round timings, problem statements, judging panel, submission process, and prizes before publishing the opportunity. Any details not yet finalized should be updated to reflect the actual event rules.

title: One Who Codes 2026 - A Portfolio Challenge
description: One Who Codes 2026 — Online Portfolio Challenge You already built it. Now show the internet you're one who codes. One Who Codes 2026 is an online portfolio challenge for developers who bring their personality, creativity, and craftsmanship to the web. Put your best portfolio on a free ONEWHO address, submit your application link through Unstop, and compete for a total prize pool of ₹30,000. ONEWHO connects a memorable address, such as yourname.isonewho.codes, to the portfolio you have already deployed. Your website stays on its existing hosting platform. Prizes First Place: ₹15,000 Second Place: ₹10,000 Third Place: ₹5,000 Every participant with a valid entry receives a certificate of participation. Eligibility and Format Open to participants from anywhere in the world, including students and working professionals. Individual participation only. Teams are not permitted. One entry per person. Participation and claiming a ONEWHO name are free. The challenge is conducted entirely online. Submit a personal portfolio website that represents your own work. How to Participate 1. Deploy Your Portfolio Build your portfolio using your preferred technologies and deploy it on a supported platform: Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Railway, Render, or Fly. 2. Claim Your ONEWHO Name Visit https://isonewho.codes/ , sign in with GitHub, choose your name, and connect your deployed portfolio URL. Your portfolio will be accessible through an address such as: yourname.isonewho.codes 3. Create Your Competition Entry Link Open the Applications section in your ONEWHO dashboard and add an application with the company name “Unstop.” This creates your submission link: https://yourname.isonewho.codes/a/unstop The application link lets you view recorded judging visits and tracked page activity in your ONEWHO dashboard. 4. Submit Through Unstop Complete your registration and submit both of the following before the deadline: Your ONEWHO application link ending in /a/unstop . The public GitHub source repository for your portfolio. Creating a ONEWHO name alone does not complete your competition entry. Your submission must also be completed on Unstop. Judging Criteria Creativity — 30%: Original ideas, personal identity, and thoughtful customization. Craft — 30%: Layout, typography, motion, visual consistency, and attention to detail. Content — 20%: How clearly your portfolio communicates who you are, what you build, and the work you have done. Performance and Accessibility — 20%: Loading experience, mobile usability, and accessibility. Rules and Guidelines Each participant may submit only one entry. ONEWHO permits one name per GitHub account. The portfolio must represent your own work. Include its public source repository, with development history associated with your GitHub account. Templates and AI tools are permitted. Judging rewards your original contribution; changing only the name on a template will not score well on creativity. You must deploy the portfolio yourself on a supported hosting platform. Portfolios automatically generated by ONEWHO from a GitHub profile are not eligible. Submit the required ONEWHO application link and public source repository through Unstop before the deadline. You may improve your portfolio until submissions close. After the deadline, leave the submitted website unchanged until results are announced. Keep your ONEWHO address connected to your portfolio and publicly accessible throughout judging and until results are announced. All entries must comply with ONEWHO’s acceptable use policy: https://isonewho.codes/acceptable-use . Entries that violate the rules or acceptable use policy may be disqualified. The judges’ decisions are final. Important Dates Registration Opens: 1 November 2026 Registration and Submission Deadline: 15 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST Judging: 16–17 November 2026 Results Announced: 18 November 2026 All dates and times follow India Standard Time (IST).

title: Agents that act. Systems that answer. | Free Virtual Agentic-AI Hackathon

How Projects Are Judged: We judge how your project behaves when things go wrong: Failure modes: how does it break? Human oversight: who stays in the loop? Intervention: can someone stop it? Key Dates: Registration closes: Nov 27 Hackathon: Nov 28–30 (virtual) Final results: Dec 8 Who Can Join: Students worldwide, solo or in teams of 1–4. Free.

description: Overview Innovate. Build. Break Barriers. The hackathon provides a platform for students to collaborate, think creatively, explore emerging technologies, and develop innovative solutions to real-world problems. Whether you are a coder, designer, researcher, or aspiring entrepreneur, this is your opportunity to showcase your skills, experiment with technology, and bring your ideas to life. Work in teams, tackle challenging problem statements, build functional prototypes, and compete with fellow innovators. Push your limits, learn from the experience, and turn your imagination into innovation! Domains Participants can explore innovative solutions across the following domains: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning (AI/ML): Intelligent systems, predictive analytics, automation, generative AI, and AI-powered applications. Web Development: Innovative websites, web applications, SaaS platforms, and digital solutions. Mobile Application Development: Android/iOS applications, cross-platform solutions, and mobile-first innovations. Blockchain & Web3: Decentralized applications, smart contracts, digital identity, and secure transactions. Cybersecurity: Network security, threat detection, data privacy, and secure digital infrastructure. Internet of Things (IoT): Smart devices, automation, connected systems, and sensor-based solutions. Healthcare & MedTech: Healthcare accessibility, patient management, medical innovation, and wellness solutions. FinTech: Digital payments, financial inclusion, banking solutions, and financial automation. Sustainability & Smart Cities: Environmental solutions, waste management, energy efficiency, and smart infrastructure. Open Innovation: Any technology-driven solution addressing a meaningful real-world problem. Participation Guidelines Participation is open to eligible college students. Participants must register within the specified registration deadline. Teams may consist of 2–4 members . Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged. Each team must nominate one team leader as the primary point of contact. All team members must be registered successfully. Hackathon Rules & Regulations All projects must be developed during the designated hackathon period. Pre-existing projects cannot be submitted as original hackathon solutions. However, previously developed libraries, frameworks, and open-source tools may be used. Teams must develop solutions relevant to the selected domain or assigned problem statement. Plagiarism, duplication, and misrepresentation of work will result in disqualification. Teams must submit their source code, project documentation, and working prototype within the stipulated deadline. Participants must ensure that their projects are functional and demonstrable during evaluation. Any use of AI tools, APIs, third-party libraries, and open-source resources must be appropriately acknowledged. Teams must maintain professional conduct throughout the event. The decision of the judging panel and organizing committee will be final. Organizers reserve the right to modify the event schedule, rules, or guidelines when necessary. Evaluation Criteria Projects will be evaluated based on the following parameters: Innovation & Originality: 20% Technical Implementation: 25% Problem Relevance & Impact: 20% Functionality & Execution: 20% Presentation & Pitch: 15% Project Submission Requirements Each team must submit: Project title and selected domain. Problem statement and proposed solution. Working prototype or Minimum Viable Product (MVP). Source code repository (GitHub or equivalent). Project presentation (PPT). Brief documentation explaining the implementation, technology stack, and future scope. Demonstration of the working solution. What to Expect An opportunity to transform ideas into real-world solutions. Hands-on experience with emerging technologies. Networking and collaboration with fellow innovators. Expert evaluation and feedback. Recognition, certificates, and exciting prizes for outstanding teams. Important Note Participants are expected to bring their own laptops and any additional hardware required for their projects. Further information regarding the venue, schedule, problem statements, submission deadlines, and other event-specific instructions will be communicated by the organizing committee. Organized by ISTE TCET Think Beyond. Build Beyond. Innovate Beyond.

title: WebClone Mania
description: Event Overview WebCloneMania is a web development competition designed to test participants' frontend development, debugging, and problem-solving skills. The event will feature two segments: Beginner and Advanced , allowing participants to compete based on their skill levels. Beginner Segment – Website Recreation: Participants will recreate a reference website revealed by the organisers at the beginning of the competition, focusing on visual accuracy, responsiveness, and functionality. Advanced Segment – Debug and Deploy: Participants will receive a pre-written codebase containing bugs, incomplete features, and backend issues. They must identify and fix the issues, implement the required functionality, and ensure the application works as intended. Eligibility and Participation Participation is individual; team formation is not permitted. Students from any college are eligible to participate. Participants from any academic year or specialization may participate. Participants must register for the appropriate segment according to the registration instructions provided by the organisers. Each participant may compete individually and must submit their own work. Segment 1: Beginner – Website Recreation Format Participants will be shown a reference website on the spot and must recreate it within the allotted time. Rules The reference website will be revealed immediately before the challenge begins. Participants will have approximately 3–4 hours to complete the challenge, subject to the final schedule announced by the organisers. Participants may use HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Next.js, or other permitted frontend technologies. AI tools, coding assistants, libraries, frameworks, and official documentation are permitted. Participants must develop their own implementation during the competition. Submitting a pre-built clone or copying another participant's work is prohibited. Unauthorised external assistance is not permitted. The final website must be functional and accessible for evaluation. Submission Requirements Each participant must submit: Source Code: A GitHub repository containing the complete project. Live Website: A deployed website link or clear instructions to run the project locally. Demonstration Video: A short video demonstrating the completed website. Participant Details: Name, registration details, and other information requested by the organisers. All submissions must be completed before the announced deadline. Segment 2: Advanced – Debug and Deploy Format Participants will receive an existing codebase containing intentional bugs, broken functionality, incomplete implementations, or backend integration issues. Their task is to analyse the code, identify the problems, implement the required fixes, and make the application work correctly. Rules The starter codebase and problem statement will be provided by the organisers at the beginning of the challenge. Participants will have approximately 3–4 hours to debug, implement, test, and demonstrate their solutions. The codebase may include frontend, backend, database, API integration, authentication, or other web application components. Participants must identify and fix the issues in the provided code rather than replace the entire project with an unrelated implementation. Participants may use permitted programming languages, frameworks, debugging tools, AI coding assistants, and official documentation. Participants must understand and be able to explain their changes during evaluation. Unauthorised external assistance, copying another participant's solution, or sharing solutions during the competition is prohibited. The final application must run successfully and satisfy the requirements specified in the problem statement. Participants must submit their corrected codebase and demonstrate the working application before the deadline. Submission Requirements Each participant must submit: Source Code: A GitHub repository containing the corrected project. Working Application: A live deployment, where feasible, or a locally running application for evaluation. Demonstration: A short video or live demonstration showing the fixes and working features. Participant Details: Name, registration details, and other information requested by the organisers. Evaluation Criteria Beginner Segment Visual similarity to the reference website. Layout, typography, colours, and styling. Responsiveness across screen sizes. Functional interactions and navigation. Code quality and overall completeness. Advanced Segment Correct identification and resolution of bugs. Successful implementation of required features. Frontend–backend integration and API functionality. Application stability, error handling, and testing. Code quality, efficiency, and completeness. Ability to explain the implemented fixes. The organisers will announce the final scoring weights and evaluation procedure at the event. Fair Play and Disqualification Copying another participant's work or submitting someone else's implementation is prohibited. Unauthorised collaboration or external assistance is not allowed. Participants must not interfere with another participant's system, code, or submission. Misrepresenting work or exploiting the evaluation process may result in disqualification. The organisers reserve the right to disqualify participants who violate the rules. General Instructions Participants must bring their own laptops and ensure their development environments are ready. Participants should arrive at the venue before the scheduled start time. Internet access will be provided subject to availability. The organisers will communicate the exact timings, problem statements, submission links, and scoring weights before the competition begins. All decisions made by the organising team regarding the conduct and evaluation of the event will be final.

description: Boeing–IIT National Aeromodelling Competition 2025–26 | IIT Madras Zone About the Competition The challenge is to design, build, and operate a radio-controlled fixed-wing aircraft capable of carrying the maximum possible payload relative to its own weight and delivering it accurately to a designated drop zone. The abstract will be evaluated to shortlist teams for the zonal competition. Submission requirements: An A4-format design abstract of no more than 15 pages. Standard formatting with 1.5 line spacing. Technical details of the aircraft, including dimensions, wing area, and velocity. An explanation of how the design addresses the competition problem statement. A ZIP file containing 5–10 photographs of the aircraft during construction. The abstract must be submitted at least 20 days before the zonal competition date. Shortlisted teams will be announced 15 days before the event, according to the published competition guidelines. Stage 2: Zonal Competition – IIT Madras Shortlisted teams will bring their aircraft and necessary equipment to compete in two rounds. Round 1: Qualifier Round The objective is to demonstrate safe flight while carrying a payload and achieve a high payload-to-aircraft weight ratio. The organiser-provided payload consists of golf balls weighing 45 g each. The aircraft must carry the payload for a minimum of 30 seconds. The payload must be carried inside the aircraft and must not be externally exposed. The aircraft must complete the attempt within a maximum of 3 minutes from take-off to landing. Each team receives two attempts, and the better score is considered. Scoring formula: Score = (Weight of payload carried × 100) / Weight of aircraft without payload. Aircraft that cannot maintain flight for 30 seconds with the payload receive zero points. The top 30 teams based on the qualifier scores advance to the Main Round. Teams qualifying for the Main Round are eligible for a reimbursement of ₹5,000 per team towards aircraft material costs, subject to the competition’s stated requirements. Round 2: Main Round – Payload Delivery Challenge Teams must demonstrate their aircraft’s payload-carrying capability and accurate payload release. Carry independent golf balls as payload. Fly for at least 30 seconds before releasing the payload. Release all payloads in a single drop using one transmitter channel. Deliver the payload into a circular drop zone of 20 m diameter. The drop zone is located 40 m from the take-off and landing zone. Complete the attempt within the maximum 3-minute time limit. Payloads must fall as separate golf balls. Combining them into one larger payload or releasing them inside a common box is not permitted. Each team receives two attempts, and the better score is considered. Scoring formula: Score = (Weight of payload successfully dropped inside the zone × 100) / Weight of aircraft without payload. National Finals The top three teams from the IIT Madras Zonal Competition will be invited to the national finals at IIT Delhi, according to the 2025–26 competition guidelines. The final-round problem statement will be announced separately by the organisers. Eligibility Criteria Only students are eligible to participate. Each team must have a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 4 student members. An additional mentor may accompany the team but cannot assist during competition participation. Team members may belong to the same or different educational institutions, provided all institutions fall within the same designated zone. Each participant can be a member of only one team. Participants must carry a valid college or school ID card and a bona fide certificate signed by the respective HoD, Dean, or Principal. Each team can participate in only one zonal event. Aircraft Design Constraints Aircraft type: A self-designed and fabricated fixed-wing radio-controlled aircraft is mandatory. Ready-to-fly, almost-ready-to-fly, and bind-and-fly models are not permitted. Maximum aircraft weight: 800 g without payload. Maximum wingspan: 1 metre. Maximum propeller diameter: 13 inches. Thrust-to-weight ratio: Must not exceed 1.5 without payload. Power source: Electric motors only. Internal combustion engines and other thrust sources are prohibited. Flight control: Gyroscopes, receiver programming assistance, and programmed mission steps are prohibited. Flight assistance: FPV and other flying-support systems are not allowed. Payload mechanism: The payload must be securely mounted and comply with the prescribed round-specific release requirements. Aircraft consistency: The same aircraft must be used in both rounds and must match the design submitted in the abstract. General Rules and Safety Regulations Teams must bring their aircraft and all required equipment. Aircraft systems, including motors and servos, will be inspected before participation. All aircraft must use 2.4 GHz radio unless another frequency has been approved in advance by the organisers. Receivers must operate in receiver-only mode. Metal propellers are prohibited. Teams must not share aircraft components with other teams. Powered take-off with landing gear or a manual ground-level launch is permitted. Damaged aircraft may be repaired, but replacement aircraft are not permitted. Pilots must remain within the designated flying zone. Flying outside the permitted zone may result in disqualification. Participants must follow all safety instructions from judges and organisers. A safety pilot may take control when required for safety. Teams must be ready when called for their attempt; failure to do so may result in losing their turn. The same team members must participate in the national finals if their team qualifies. Attempts to unfairly influence scoring or disrupt the competition may result in immediate disqualification. If multiple teams from the same institution participate, their aircraft designs must be distinct. The 2025–26 guidelines specify a minimum 2.5% difference in wingspan, chord, and fuselage length between such teams. Scoring and Evaluation The final zonal score is calculated as follows: Final Score = (0.25 × Qualifier Round Score) + (0.75 × Main Round Score). The Main Round contributes 75% of the final score, making payload delivery performance the most significant scoring component. The top three teams with the highest final scores will be declared zonal winners. In case of a tie, a separate round may be conducted by the judges, whose decisions will be final. Prizes IIT Madras Zonal Competition First Prize: ₹50,000. Second Prize: ₹25,000. Third Prize: ₹15,000. and the remaing top 24 teams will be awarded 5000/- National Competition First Prize: ₹1,00,000. Second Prize: ₹50,000. Third Prize: ₹30,000. The top three teams from each zonal competition will be invited to the national finals at IIT Delhi.

AGENTX 2.0
description: AGENTX 2.0 is a national-level hackathon organized by HackQube, bringing together students, developers, AI enthusiasts, and innovators to build intelligent, technology-driven solutions to real-world challenges. The hackathon focuses on Artificial Intelligence, AI Agents, Agentic AI, Generative AI, and intelligent automation. Participants will have the opportunity to transform ideas into functional prototypes that demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, practical applicability, and real-world impact. Participants must select one of the official problem statements and develop a solution that addresses the specified challenge. Eligibility Criteria Students enrolled in recognized colleges or universities are eligible to participate. Developers, AI enthusiasts, and aspiring innovators may participate, subject to the registration requirements. Participants must provide accurate information during registration. All participants must comply with the hackathon rules and submission guidelines. Team Formation Rules Team Size: 2–4 members per team. Inter-college Teams: Allowed. Team members may belong to different colleges or universities. Inter-specialization Teams: Allowed. Members from different academic disciplines and technical specializations may collaborate. Each participant may be part of only one team. Teams must provide accurate details for all members during registration. One team must submit only one project for evaluation. Official Problem Statements Teams must select one of the following eight problem statements and develop a solution aligned with its objectives. PS01: Agentic Workflow Automation Build an AI agent that automates repetitive tasks by planning multi-step workflows, integrating external tools and APIs, executing actions, and verifying task completion. PS02: Autonomous AI Software Engineer Develop an AI agent that analyzes codebases, identifies bugs, proposes fixes, runs tests, and generates actionable reports to improve software development workflows. PS03: Multi-Agent Research & Fact-Checking Create a multi-agent system that researches complex topics, verifies information using reliable sources, identifies conflicting claims, and generates evidence-backed reports. PS04: Personalized AI Learning Agent Build an intelligent learning agent that identifies knowledge gaps, creates personalized learning paths, generates assessments, and adapts recommendations based on student progress. PS05: AI Operations Agent for Businesses Develop an AI agent that streamlines business operations by analyzing data, managing routine workflows, identifying exceptions, and recommending actions with appropriate human oversight. PS06: AI-Powered Cybersecurity Triage Create a defensive AI agent that analyzes security logs, correlates alerts, detects suspicious activities, and recommends safe remediation steps. PS07: Smart Energy & Sustainability Agent Build an AI agent that analyzes energy consumption data, identifies inefficiencies, predicts potential wastage, and recommends actionable sustainability improvements. PS08: Startup Co-Pilot Agent Develop a multi-agent system that assists early-stage founders with market research, competitor analysis, customer profiling, idea validation, and execution planning. Competition Format The competition will follow the official schedule and format announced by HackQube. The proposed process includes: Registration: Eligible participants register through Unstop in teams of 2–4 members. Problem Statement Selection: Each team selects one official problem statement from PS01 to PS08. Solution Development: Teams design and develop their solutions using appropriate technologies, APIs, frameworks, and AI tools. Project Submission: Teams submit the required project details and demonstration materials before the official deadline. Evaluation: Judges assess projects according to the published evaluation criteria. Final Results: Winners are determined based on evaluation scores and the final decision of the judging panel. The round-wise schedule, duration, submission deadline, and grand finale details will be communicated through official event announcements. Project Submission Guidelines Each team must submit the materials specified by the organizers. These may include: Project title and selected problem statement. Problem overview and proposed solution. Key features and explanation of the approach. Working prototype or functional demonstration. Source-code repository link, if required. Presentation or pitch deck, if required. Technology stack, APIs, frameworks, and AI tools used. Explanation of the solution's feasibility, impact, and scalability. All required submissions must be completed before the official deadline. Late or incomplete submissions may be disqualified. Judging Criteria Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters: Innovation: Originality and creativity of the proposed solution. Technical Implementation: Quality, functionality, and effective use of AI and other technologies. Problem Relevance: Effectiveness in addressing the selected problem statement. Feasibility and Scalability: Practical applicability and potential for further development. User Experience: Usability, accessibility, and clarity of the solution. Presentation and Demonstration: Quality of the project explanation, working demo, and responses to judges' questions. The final scoring weights and any additional evaluation requirements will be communicated by the organizers. Rules and Code of Conduct All submissions must address one of the official problem statements. Plagiarism, fraudulent registrations, misrepresentation of contributions, and presenting copied work as original are prohibited. Teams must disclose relevant third-party code, datasets, APIs, AI models, and tools used in their projects when requested. Participants must have the necessary rights and permissions to use submitted code, content, datasets, and other materials. Projects must comply with applicable laws, ethical technology practices, and data privacy requirements. Unauthorized system access, malicious activities, and misuse of data or services are strictly prohibited. Cybersecurity solutions must remain defensive and operate only within authorized environments. Teams must not submit multiple entries under different team identities unless explicitly permitted by the organizers. Participants must maintain professional conduct and respect fellow participants, mentors, judges, and organizers. The organizers reserve the right to investigate violations and disqualify teams that breach the rules. The judges' decisions will be final, subject to the published competition rules. Prizes and Recognition Prize details, certificates, special recognitions, and other benefits, if applicable, will be announced through official HackQube communications and the Unstop opportunity page. Only prizes and benefits explicitly confirmed by the organizers should be considered guaranteed. Important Information Opportunity: AGENTX 2.0 — National-Level Hackathon Organizer: HackQube Registration Platform: Unstop Team Size: 2–4 members Inter-college Participation: Allowed Inter-specialization Participation: Allowed Problem Statements: 8 Competition Format: As announced by the organizers Event Date: 14 November 2026 Venue: As announced by the organizers Registration Deadline: As announced by the organizers Participants are responsible for reviewing official announcements, completing registration correctly, and meeting all applicable deadlines. Any updates to the schedule, format, or rules will be communicated through the designated official channels. Build. Innovate. Elevate. Organized by HackQube — A Builders-First Technology Ecosystem.
